It shares nothing with PDF, ZIP or guides beyond the download helper from 19أ, and it is a text-only path: no canvas, no encode gate, no new dependency, no storage migration. Splitting it out keeps the heavy binary work from blocking a part that is nearly free.
naturalSplitPoints.verifiableBy: `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/modules/colour/export.test.ts tests/unit/modules/style-export/` — every format round-trips through a real parser (JSON.parse, a CSS custom-property regex, DTCG $value/$type presence), and the tokens output validates against the DTCG shape. Plus a verify:export case that downloads each of the four and checks the file's first bytes and extension.

naturalSplitPoints.title: 19ج — PDF وتقرير المقارنة
contains: Add pdf-lib to dependencies and build `src/modules/export/pdf.ts`: single and multi-page, correct page size and orientation, Arabic font embedding for the metadata
A PDF byte-inspector test helper — the analogue of tests/helpers/png-chunks.ts: %PDF- header, %%EOF, and Info-dictionary key enumeration, so the metadata claim is proven on bytes not on intent
Make stripMetadataOnExport actually strip: suppress pdf-lib's default Producer/Creator/CreationDate/ModDate, and strip url/title/project from generated filenames
The compare report as a real document: diff image + percentage + region list + both captures' metadata, wiring the disabled button at src/pages/compare/parts/Header.tsx:47
Widening the LiveDiff contract (src/shared/messaging/contract.ts:68) so region BOXES cross the wire, not just the count — the gap Phase_17.md:86-90 declares
naturalSplitPoints.whyThisBoundary: PDF is where this phase's security claim becomes real. Everything before it has nothing to strip; pdf-lib is the first writer that stamps product metadata into a file by default, so the byte-inspector and the strip toggle must land together with it. The compare report rides along because it is the phase's first multi-element DOCUMENT and PDF is its natural container — and because its blocker (region boxes never crossing the wire) is a contract change, better done once next to the document work than twice. This part is entirely outside the MVP gate (§4: «PDF · الأدلة · تصديرات المطوّر» all deferred to v1.0), so it can be sequenced after the gate without holding anything up.
naturalSplitPoints.verifiableBy: `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/modules/export/pdf.test.ts` asserting on real bytes: %PDF- magic, %%EOF terminator, page count and MediaBox dimensions, and — with stripMetadata on — that the Info dictionary contains no Producer, no CreationDate, and no occurrence of the source url/title/project name anywhere in the byte stream. Plus a verify:export case opening the exported compare report and reading its region count against the live diff.

naturalSplitPoints.title: 19د — دليل الخطوات بصيغه الأربع + قوالب التصدير
contains: Extend GuideRecord with per-step captions and explicit order; DB_VERSION 2→3 migration in src/shared/storage/migrations.ts
A guide authoring surface and a real creation path (today `guides.put` is only ever called to reassign projectId; the library's guide card opens `noopOpen`)
Numbered PDF in correct RTL order — human Eastern-Arabic ordinals per §3.5, reusing the ordinal logic of src/modules/editor/pins.ts
Sequential images in a ZIP — needs a store-only ZIP writer (no dependency exists; scripts/zip.mjs shells out to the `zip` CLI and is Node-only)
Markdown with base64-embedded or sidecar images
The self-contained shareable HTML page: single file, zero external dependencies, correct RTL, opens with no network
Saved export templates (قوالب التصدير)
Lighthouse ≥95 on Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices for the exported page — the only Lighthouse task in the whole phase (Rasd_Plan.md:193)
naturalSplitPoints.whyThisBoundary: The step guide is the one part that needs a STORAGE MIGRATION and a new authoring UI, not just an encoder — GuideRecord today has no place to put a step's text. It is also the only part carrying a Lighthouse gate, and that gate is in real tension with the single-file base64 requirement, so it deserves its own measurement pass rather than being appended to another part's Gate B. Export templates land here because templates can only be designed once every option they must capture exists — and by this point they all do.
naturalSplitPoints.verifiableBy: A verify:export case that opens the exported standalone HTML with the network blocked (CDP Network.emulateNetworkConditions offline) and asserts every reports naturalWidth>0 and the console is clean; a Lighthouse run on that same file asserting ≥95 in all three categories; `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/modules/export/guide.test.ts` asserting RTL ordinal order and that the ZIP's central directory lists exactly N entries in step order; plus a migration test proving a DB_VERSION 2 database with existing guides upgrades without data loss.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «الشاشات `export / modal` و`export / done` منفَّذة» is listed under التنفيذ as a deliverable, and «بصري: export / modal و export / done تُقارَنان بإطاري Figma 73:2 و129:1249» under الاختبارات.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: The two Figma node ids exist nowhere in the repository other than those two plan lines. There is no frame export, no screenshot, no inventory entry, no design token reference tying them to anything. This is the identical situation Phase 15 hit and resolved by deferring its own three frames (70:2, 99:415, 128:133) to Phase 26.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: `grep -rn '73:2|129:1249|export / modal|export / done' Rasd_Plan.md Docs/` returns exactly two lines, both from Rasd_Plan.md itself. Compare Docs/Phases/Phase_15.md:95: «المقارنة البصرية بإطارات Figma 70:2 · 99:415 · 128:133 | لم تجرِ. المعرّفات الثلاثة لا تظهر في المستودع خارج سطر الخطّة نفسه … | المرحلة 26».

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: The phase is described as needing metadata stripping «من الملف نفسه لا من العرض فقط، ويُتحقَّق بفحص بايتات الملف» — framed as the phase's security claim, and §2 justifies assigning Sonnet 5 to the phase precisely because «الادّعاء محكوم باختبار بوّابة يفحص بايتات الملف».
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: For the formats inside the MVP gate (PNG, and WebP once added) there is currently nothing to strip, and this is already PROVEN on live bytes. bake.ts writes no url, title, date, browser info or project name into the file; Chrome's convertToBlob emits no tEXt/iTXt/zTXt/eXIf; and a live guard already asserts exactly that. The metadata risk does not exist until pdf-lib (which stamps Producer/CreationDate by default), the standalone HTML guide (which embeds url/title by design), and download filenames exist — all of which are v1.0, outside the MVP gate. Shipping the toggle against PNG alone would be a no-op that reads as an implemented security feature.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: src/modules/editor/bake.ts:374 is the whole encode: `const blob = await target.encodeTarget.convertToBlob({ type: 'image/png' })` — no metadata written anywhere in the file. scripts/verify-editor.mjs:1275-1280 already runs the byte check against a real exported file in Chrome and passes: «ولا مقاطع بيانات وصفية — المقاطع: …». tests/unit/modules/editor/png-chunks.test.ts:53 asserts `metadataChunks(parsePng(CLEAN))` is `[]`.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «حذف البيانات الوصفية» is listed in the dependency table as depending on 15 and being ✅ inside the MVP gate, i.e. a shippable MVP feature.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «تصديرات المطوّر: CSS · JSON · Tailwind · Design Tokens (W3C) — من لوحة الألوان ومن بيانات الفحص» is written as one undifferentiated bullet, and the dependency table gives it a single row depending on «13 و14».

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: The phase's المهام/التنفيذ section lists the step guide as one bullet with four formats, at the same altitude as «الحافظة» or «PDF»; the الوحدات line implies it is one file, `src/modules/export/guide.ts`.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: The dependency table asserts «الاعتماد على 17 يخصّ تقرير المقارنة فقط — ولا يحجب أجزاء MVP», implying Phase 17 being complete is sufficient for the compare report.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.claimLocation: Rasd_Plan.md, المرحلة 19 dependency table and the sentence following it
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: Phase 17 being ✅ COMPLETE is necessary but not sufficient. Phase 17's own closing doc declares that the region LIST — one of the four things the plan says the report must contain («صورة الفرق + النسبة + قائمة المناطق + بيانات اللقطتين») — is computed in the background and then discarded before crossing the message wire. So Phase 19 cannot assemble the report from what Phase 17 exposes; it must widen the LiveDiff contract first.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: Docs/Phases/Phase_17.md:86-90: «مستطيل التظليل فوق مصغَّرة المعرض. LiveDiff يحمل عدد المناطق لا صناديقها — تُحسب في الخلفية ثمّ تُختزَل قبل عبور السلك. رسمُه يحتاج توسيع العقد؛ لم يُبنَ ولم يُدَّعَ.» The contract type is at src/shared/messaging/contract.ts:68 `export interface LiveDiff`.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «التنزيل (§9.2): PNG WebP PDF، بخيارات الجودة والدقة (1× / 2×)» — written as plumbing, and §2 assigns Sonnet 5 on the grounds that the phase is «سباكة صيغ محدَّدة».
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: Adding a second image format is not free plumbing: it collides with an architecturally enforced invariant. ADR 0015's single-encode-exit is enforced by three ESLint AST selectors that ban `toBlob`/`convertToBlob`/`toDataURL` by dotted call, by computed member access, AND by bare string literal, with a four-file allowlist that is itself asserted by a unit test running ESLint on fixtures. Any WebP or PDF raster encode either lives inside bake.ts or requires amending ENCODE_ALLOWED — which the eslint config's own header calls a decision that «يحتاج ADR، لا تعديل سطر» in spirit (the same language the forbidden-permissions list uses).
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: eslint.config.js:231, :236, :241 (the three selectors), `ENCODE_ALLOWED = ['src/modules/editor/bake.ts','src/background/image-ops.ts','src/background/stitch.ts','src/pages/library/thumbnail-encoder.ts']`, and tests/unit/architecture-boundaries.test.ts which imports ENCODE_ALLOWED and encodeSelectors and runs ESLint to prove violations are raised at severity 2.

openQuestions: Page or modal? The التنفيذ line says «الشاشات export / modal و export / done منفَّذة» (a modal) while the الوحدات line says `src/pages/export/` (a page). These cost different things: a page means four coordinated edits (src/shared/page-paths.ts PAGE_PATHS, vite.config.ts rollupOptions.input, the manifest/verify-dist comparison, and the `page/open` PageName union), a modal means building it inside editor + library + compare or hoisting a shared overlay component. This should be decided in 19أ, once, before any later part inherits it.

Does WebP encoding go inside bake.ts (parameterising the hardcoded 'image/png' at src/modules/editor/bake.ts:374) or into a new file added to ENCODE_ALLOWED? The first keeps the four-file allowlist intact and is the cheaper read of ADR 0015; the second is cleaner separation but amends an invariant that a unit test asserts. Needs an explicit call, arguably an ADR amendment.

Where does the «الرفض يُحترَم ولا يُعاد سؤاله في الجلسة نفسها» memory for a denied `downloads` request live? The service worker is not a durable session and can be terminated at any time; chrome.storage.session, an in-memory map in the page, and a settings field all behave differently across a worker restart. No session-scoped denial memory exists anywhere in the repo today.

Can the standalone HTML guide hit Lighthouse ≥95 on Performance while being a single file with base64-embedded images and no external dependencies? These pull against each other directly — base64 rasters inflate the document and delay LCP. If it cannot, the plan's own Lighthouse target (Rasd_Plan.md:176, :193 — the only Lighthouse task in the phase) needs renegotiating before 19د starts, not at its Gate B.

Are the Figma frames 73:2 and 129:1249 actually reachable? They appear nowhere in the repo. Either fetch them at the start of 19أ, or declare the visual comparison deferred to Phase 26 up front — the precedent Phase 15 set (Docs/Phases/Phase_15.md:95).

Phase_14.md:196 explicitly hands this phase an open decision and asks that it not be answered silently: when the new export screen is built, does the fourth «نص قابل للنسخ» format get added to PalettePanel as well, or does it stay confined to the in-page extraction panel?

ZIP: hand-roll a store-only (uncompressed) ZIP writer inside src/modules/export/, or add fflate/jszip as a second new dependency alongside pdf-lib? A store-only writer is perhaps 120 lines with a CRC32 that ALREADY EXISTS in the repo (tests/helpers/png-chunks.ts exports `crc32`) — but it currently lives under tests/ and would need promoting to src/shared/ to be reusable by production code.

Arabic in PDF: pdf-lib does not shape or bidi-order Arabic text. Does «مع دعم العربية في البيانات الوصفية» mean only the PDF Info dictionary strings (which are UTF-16BE and need no shaping — cheap), or also rendered Arabic captions on the numbered guide pages (which needs an embedded font plus a shaping pass — expensive)? The plan's wording says البيانات الوصفية, which suggests the cheap reading, but the numbered step guide with notes implies the expensive one.
